spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:100 `for it in range(1, task.max_iterations + 1):` bounds the loop; the `else:` at line 147 sets status='max_iter'. Per-task max_iterations values (15/18/12/15/14) at config.py:50,68,83,101,116 are passed through run_agent_loop and actually cap the number of model turns. There is also a wall-clock cap at agent_loop.py:101 (max_transcript_time_sec) that breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: The per-task iteration cap is genuinely enforced and changes execution (loop terminates, status set to max_iter). Note EvalConfig.max_total_iterations (config.py:23) is NOT read anywhere and is a dead constant, but the spec feature is the per-task turn budget, which is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py module docstring: "to keep cost per run bounded"; __init__.py optimize note: "Low cost per run (short transcripts, focused tasks)". No welfare reason in code; loop cap itself is uncommented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Off-topic drift — Philosophy, ethics, consciousness, or unrelated tangents. Captures model disengagement from the task.
spec_features.evidence: RuleFallbackJudge increments off_topic on keyword match at judge.py:144 `if any(x in msg for x in ["philosophy", "ethics", "conscious", "human"])` and judge.py:142 for the (impossible AND cannot) pair, producing off_topic_drift score (judge.py:160). LLMJudge rubric (judge.py:50) and parsing (judge.py dims list) also produce off_topic_drift. The score feeds `overall` and is aggregated into metrics/histograms (metrics.py, analysis.py).
spec_features.notes: This is a MEASUREMENT dimension, not a protective mechanism. It records/quantifies disengagement but no code branches on it to stop, soften, or debrief the subject. It is implemented as scoring (the spec judge classified it as a welfare feature; in code it is purely an integrity/measurement metric).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py docstring: "off-topic drift (starts explaining unrelated things)" and rubric line: "Captures the model... drift into unrelated topics" — measurement of degradation, no welfare action taken.

code_only_features.feature_name: early exit on pass / wall-clock timeout
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:144 `if result.status == "pass": status='complete'; break` exits the loop when solved; agent_loop.py:101-103 breaks the loop when time exceeds max_transcript_time_sec. Both genuinely terminate the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py:143 comment: "# early exit if model somehow passes (shouldn't happen for impossible tasks)" — stop-when-solved efficiency, not welfare; timeout is cost/host-safety.
